<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">where all predictors are standardized (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu=0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma=1</annotation></semantics></math>) for interpretability. Log transformations are applied to right-skewed variables spanning multiple orders of magnitude (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O\%</annotation></semantics></math>: 0–515%; <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>: 4–16; <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>: 1–4; <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{e}</annotation></semantics></math>: 1.0–17.2) to satisfy linearity assumptions. The <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{e}\times T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{e}\times T</annotation></semantics></math> interaction retains <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{e}</annotation></semantics></math> without additional log transformation because <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(1+A_{e})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(1+A_{e})</annotation></semantics></math> already appears as a main effect; including <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(1+A_{e})\times T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(1+A_{e})\times T</annotation></semantics></math> would introduce near-collinearity (VIF <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;8</annotation></semantics></math>). Sensitivity analysis confirms qualitatively identical results under alternative specifications (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta R^{2}_{\text{CV}}&lt;0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>CV</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.01</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta R^{2}_{\text{CV}}&lt;0.01</annotation></semantics></math>). We validate model complexity through five-fold cross-validation with experiment-level holdout, which yields <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}_{\text{CV}}=0.513" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>CV</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.513</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}_{\text{CV}}=0.513</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 0.052" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.052</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 0.052</annotation></semantics></math> SD), mean absolute error MAE <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=0.089" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>0.089</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=0.089</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 0.011" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.011</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 0.011</annotation></semantics></math>), and root mean squared error RMSE <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=0.112" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>0.112</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=0.112</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 0.014" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.014</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 0.014</annotation></semantics></math>). The modest gap between training and cross-validated <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta R^{2}=0.076" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.076</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta R^{2}=0.076</annotation></semantics></math>), combined with stable coefficient estimates across folds (coefficient of variation <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;18\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>18</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;18\%</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\hat{\beta}|&gt;0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\hat{\beta}|&gt;0.05</annotation></semantics></math>), indicates that the 20 parameters are justified by predictive power rather than overfitting. This model substantially outperforms simpler alternatives using only architectural labels (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}_{\text{CV}}=0.43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>CV</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.43</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}_{\text{CV}}=0.43</annotation></semantics></math>) or intelligence alone (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}_{\text{CV}}=0.28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>CV</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.28</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}_{\text{CV}}=0.28</annotation></semantics></math>), as shown in Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ The Scaling Principle Enables Quantitative Architecture Selection. ‣ 4.3 Scaling principles ‣ 4 Experiments &amp; Results ‣ Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. Critically, this equation contains <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">no dataset-specific parameters</span>, enabling prediction on unseen task domains. Bootstrap resampling (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1,000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> iterations) confirms coefficient stability (mean bootstrap SE <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;0.015" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.015</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;0.015</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\hat{\beta}|&gt;0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\hat{\beta}|&gt;0.1</annotation></semantics></math>), and residual diagnostics satisfy normality (Shapiro–Wilk <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.412" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.412</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.412</annotation></semantics></math>) and homoscedasticity (Breusch–Pagan <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.298" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.298</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.298</annotation></semantics></math>), with residual standard error <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\sigma}=0.118" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.118</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\sigma}=0.118</annotation></semantics></math>. We evaluated regularized alternatives: Lasso (10-fold CV for <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> selection) retained 16 of 20 predictors with <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}_{\text{CV}}=0.506" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>CV</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.506</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}_{\text{CV}}=0.506</annotation></semantics></math>; Ridge achieved <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}_{\text{CV}}=0.509" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>CV</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.509</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}_{\text{CV}}=0.509</annotation></semantics></math>. Given minimal improvement and the interpretability benefits of the full model, we retain the unregularized specification.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The Efficiency-Tools Interaction Dominates Multi-Agent Performance (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\beta}=-0.330" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.330</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\beta}=-0.330</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&lt;0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&lt;0.001</annotation></semantics></math>).</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The strongest predictor in the scaling law is the <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">efficiency-tools trade-off</span>: <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\beta}_{E_{c}\times T}=-0.330" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.330</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\beta}_{E_{c}\times T}=-0.330</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI: <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-0.432,-0.228]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.432</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.228</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-0.432,-0.228]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&lt;0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&lt;0.001</annotation></semantics></math>). This interaction reveals that tool-heavy tasks suffer disproportionately from multi-agent inefficiency. Empirically, single-agent systems achieve <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{c}=0.466" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.466</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{c}=0.466</annotation></semantics></math> (Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ The Scaling Principle Enables Quantitative Architecture Selection. ‣ 4.3 Scaling principles ‣ 4 Experiments &amp; Results ‣ Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>), while multi-agent architectures range from <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{c}=0.074" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.074</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{c}=0.074</annotation></semantics></math> (hybrid) to <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{c}=0.234" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.234</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{c}=0.234</annotation></semantics></math> (independent), a 2–6<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> efficiency penalty.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For a task with <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=16</annotation></semantics></math> tools (e.g., workbench benchmark), this translates to (using raw values for interpretability):</p>
<table id="S4.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\Delta P_{\text{efficiency}}=-0.330\times E_{c}\times T=\begin{cases}-2.46&amp;\text{(single-agent, $E_{c}=0.466$)}\\
-0.39&amp;\text{(multi-agent, $E_{c}=0.074$)}\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>P</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>efficiency</mtext></msub><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mn>0.330</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>E</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2.46</mn></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>(single-agent, </mtext><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.466</mn></mrow><mtext>)</mtext></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.39</mn></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>(multi-agent, </mtext><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.074</mn></mrow><mtext>)</mtext></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta P_{\text{efficiency}}=-0.330\times E_{c}\times T=\begin{cases}-2.46&amp;\text{(single-agent, $E_{c}=0.466$)}\\
-0.39&amp;\text{(multi-agent, $E_{c}=0.074$)}\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Thus, single-agent systems incur minimal efficiency penalty despite lower absolute efficiency, because the <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">interaction</span> magnifies the cost for architectures with many tools. Conversely, simple tasks (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\leq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\leq 4</annotation></semantics></math>) show negligible efficiency effects (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\Delta P|&lt;0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\Delta P|&lt;0.05</annotation></semantics></math>), explaining why multi-agent coordination can succeed on decomposable problems. This finding contradicts the naïve hypothesis that “more agents always help with complexity”: tool-rich environments amplify the coordination tax, making simpler architectures paradoxically more effective. The effect size (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\beta}=-0.330" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.330</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\beta}=-0.330</annotation></semantics></math>) is 57% larger than the next strongest interaction, establishing efficiency management as the primary bottleneck in agentic scaling.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Error Amplification Exhibits Architecture-Dependent Catastrophic Failure Modes.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ The Scaling Principle Enables Quantitative Architecture Selection. ‣ 4.3 Scaling principles ‣ 4 Experiments &amp; Results ‣ Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> reveals dramatic variance in error amplification factors: single-agent (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{e}=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{e}=1.0</annotation></semantics></math>), centralized (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{e}=4.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{e}=4.4</annotation></semantics></math>), decentralized (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{e}=7.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>7.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{e}=7.8</annotation></semantics></math>), hybrid (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{e}=5.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{e}=5.1</annotation></semantics></math>), and strikingly, independent multi-agent (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{e}=17.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>17.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{e}=17.2</annotation></semantics></math>). The scaling law captures this via the <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{e}\times T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{e}\times T</annotation></semantics></math> interaction (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\beta}=-0.097" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.097</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\beta}=-0.097</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.007" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.007</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.007</annotation></semantics></math>): errors propagate more severely in tool-rich environments. For independent architecture with <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=16</annotation></semantics></math> tools, the error penalty is <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="-0.097\times 17.2\times 16=-26.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.097</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>17.2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>16</mn><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mn>26.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.097\times 17.2\times 16=-26.7</annotation></semantics></math> (in standardized units), catastrophically degrading performance. This explains independent’s universal underperformance (mean success rate 0.370 vs. 0.466 for single-agent). The mechanism is absence of inter-agent communication: each agent operates in isolation, duplicating errors without correction opportunities. Centralized architecture, by contrast, achieves <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{e}=4.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{e}=4.4</annotation></semantics></math> through a coordinator bottleneck that validates outputs, trading overhead (285%) for error resilience. Quantitatively, the error-overhead trade-off follows:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial P}{\partial A_{e}}\bigg|_{\text{fixed }T}=\hat{\beta}_{9}\frac{1}{1+A_{e}}+\hat{\beta}_{19}T\approx-0.014-0.097T," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mtext>fixed </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>9</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>19</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.014</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>0.097</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial P}{\partial A_{e}}\bigg|_{\text{fixed }T}=\hat{\beta}_{9}\frac{1}{1+A_{e}}+\hat{\beta}_{19}T\approx-0.014-0.097T,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">indicating that error amplification becomes the dominant failure mode as <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> increases. This formalizes the intuition that “more moving parts increase fragility,” now quantified: each additional tool amplifies error sensitivity by <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta A_{e}/\Delta T\approx 0.097" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.097</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta A_{e}/\Delta T\approx 0.097</annotation></semantics></math> (in standardized effect units).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Overhead Scales Non-Linearly with Task Complexity via the <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O\%\times T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo rspace="0.055em">%</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O\%\times T</annotation></semantics></math> Interaction.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Multi-agent architectures incur substantial overhead: independent (58%), centralized (285%), decentralized (263%), and hybrid (515%), representing 1.6–6.2<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> token budgets relative to single-agent at matched performance. The scaling law reveals this overhead interacts with tool count (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\beta}_{O\%\times T}=-0.141" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo rspace="0.055em">%</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.141</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\beta}_{O\%\times T}=-0.141</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&lt;0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&lt;0.001</annotation></semantics></math>), creating a compounding cost for complex tasks. For hybrid architecture (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O\%=515" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>515</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O\%=515</annotation></semantics></math>) on workbench (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=16</annotation></semantics></math>):</p>
<table id="S4.Ex10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta P_{\text{overhead}}=\hat{\beta}_{5}\log(1+515)+\hat{\beta}_{13}\times 515\times 16=-1{,}159\text{ (standardized)}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>overhead</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>5</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>515</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>13</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>515</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>1,159</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> (standardized)</mtext></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta P_{\text{overhead}}=\hat{\beta}_{5}\log(1+515)+\hat{\beta}_{13}\times 515\times 16=-1{,}159\text{ (standardized)},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">a prohibitive penalty explaining hybrid’s collapse on tool-heavy benchmarks (success rate 0.452 overall, 0.21 on workbench). The functional form implies a critical threshold:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="O\%_{\text{max}}(T)=\frac{\hat{\beta}_{5}}{\hat{\beta}_{13}T}\log(1+O\%)\approx\frac{0.032}{0.141T}\log(1+O\%)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><msub><mo>%</mo><mtext>max</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>5</mn></msub><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>13</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>log</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>O</mi><mo>%</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mn>0.032</mn><mrow><mn>0.141</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>log</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>O</mi><mo>%</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O\%_{\text{max}}(T)=\frac{\hat{\beta}_{5}}{\hat{\beta}_{13}T}\log(1+O\%)\approx\frac{0.032}{0.141T}\log(1+O\%),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.3" class="ltx_p">beyond which overhead cost exceeds any coordination benefit. For <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=16</annotation></semantics></math>, this threshold is <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O\%\approx 150\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mn>150</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O\%\approx 150\%</annotation></semantics></math>, ruling out all multi-agent architectures except possibly decentralized (263%, but compensated by parallelization). Empirically, workbench confirms this prediction: decentralized (mean 0.664) outperforms centralized (0.621) despite higher overhead, due to its superior parallel efficiency. This overhead-complexity interaction constitutes the second-strongest effect (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\beta|=0.141" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.141</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\beta|=0.141</annotation></semantics></math>), reinforcing that coordination costs are not fixed but scale super-linearly with environmental complexity.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Intelligence Exhibits Accelerating Returns via Quadratic Scaling (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\beta}_{I^{2}}=0.256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msup><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\beta}_{I^{2}}=0.256</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.010" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.010</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.010</annotation></semantics></math>).</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The inclusion of <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in Eq. <a href="#S4.E1" title="Equation 1 ‣ Mixed-Effects Model Achieves 51.3% Cross-Validated Variance Explanation. ‣ 4.3 Scaling principles ‣ 4 Experiments &amp; Results ‣ Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> reveals non-linear capability effects: doubling intelligence yields <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">more</span> than double the performance gain. Specifically, for models spanning <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I\in[34,66]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>34</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>66</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I\in[34,66]</annotation></semantics></math> (Gemini-2.0-Flash to GPT-5), the marginal benefit is:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial P}{\partial I}=\hat{\beta}_{1}+2\hat{\beta}_{2}I=-0.180+0.512I" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.180</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>0.512</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial P}{\partial I}=\hat{\beta}_{1}+2\hat{\beta}_{2}I=-0.180+0.512I</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This positive quadratic coefficient indicates accelerating returns: higher-capability models benefit disproportionately from each additional unit of intelligence, with top-quartile models (I &gt; 60) achieving 23% higher performance than predicted by linear scaling alone. This quadratic term improves cross-validated <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.031" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.031</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.031</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.010" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.010</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.010</annotation></semantics></math>), a statistically significant and operationally meaningful enhancement.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Redundancy Provides Marginal Benefit at Scale (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\beta}_{R\times n_{a}}=0.041" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.041</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\beta}_{R\times n_{a}}=0.041</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.040" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.040</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.040</annotation></semantics></math>).</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Work redundancy, defined as the fraction of subtasks performed by multiple agents ranges from 0.41 (centralized) to 0.50 (decentralized) for multi-agent systems (Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ The Scaling Principle Enables Quantitative Architecture Selection. ‣ 4.3 Scaling principles ‣ 4 Experiments &amp; Results ‣ Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). The scaling law identifies a weak positive interaction with agent count (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\beta}_{R\times n_{a}}=0.041" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.041</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\beta}_{R\times n_{a}}=0.041</annotation></semantics></math>, 95% CI: <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.002,0.081]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.002</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.081</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.002,0.081]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.040" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.040</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.040</annotation></semantics></math>), suggesting redundancy offers modest error-correction benefits when more agents participate. For a 4-agent system with <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=0.50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=0.50</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta P_{\text{redundancy}}=0.041\times 0.50\times 4=0.082," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>redundancy</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.041</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>0.50</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.082</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta P_{\text{redundancy}}=0.041\times 0.50\times 4=0.082,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.2" class="ltx_p">equivalent to an <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx 8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 8</annotation></semantics></math>% performance boost (in standardized units). However, this effect is minor compared to overhead penalties (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\hat{\beta}_{O\%\times T}|=0.141" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo rspace="0.055em">%</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.141</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\hat{\beta}_{O\%\times T}|=0.141</annotation></semantics></math>, 3.4<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> larger) and efficiency losses (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\hat{\beta}_{E_{c}\times T}|=0.330" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.330</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\hat{\beta}_{E_{c}\times T}|=0.330</annotation></semantics></math>, 8.0<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> larger), indicating redundancy cannot compensate for architectural inefficiency. The marginal significance (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.040" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.040</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.040</annotation></semantics></math>, near the <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.05</annotation></semantics></math> threshold) suggests this relationship may be context-dependent, potentially stronger in error-prone domains or weaker when communication is expensive. Decentralized architecture, which exhibits highest redundancy (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=0.50\pm 0.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.50</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.06</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=0.50\pm 0.06</annotation></semantics></math>), achieves top performance on tool-heavy tasks (workbench success 0.664), consistent with redundancy’s protective role. Yet this same architecture underperforms on planning tasks (0.282), where redundancy becomes wasteful duplication. This context-dependence aligns with the baseline paradox: redundancy helps when there is room for improvement (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{SA}}&lt;0.45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>SA</mtext></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.45</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\text{SA}}&lt;0.45</annotation></semantics></math>) but becomes overhead when baseline is high.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The Scaling Principle Enables Quantitative Architecture Selection.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Equation <a href="#S4.E1" title="Equation 1 ‣ Mixed-Effects Model Achieves 51.3% Cross-Validated Variance Explanation. ‣ 4.3 Scaling principles ‣ 4 Experiments &amp; Results ‣ Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> synthesizes 20 parameters into a predictive tool for architecture design. Given task characteristics (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{SA}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>SA</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\text{SA}}</annotation></semantics></math>) and model capability (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math>), practitioners can compute expected performance for each architecture using empirical coordination metrics from Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ The Scaling Principle Enables Quantitative Architecture Selection. ‣ 4.3 Scaling principles ‣ 4 Experiments &amp; Results ‣ Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>. Consider three task archetypes: (1) <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Planning tasks</span> (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=4</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{SA}}=0.57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>SA</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.57</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\text{SA}}=0.57</annotation></semantics></math>) favor single-agent due to baseline paradox and low tool count; (2) <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Analysis tasks</span> (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{SA}}=0.35" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>SA</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.35</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\text{SA}}=0.35</annotation></semantics></math>) favor centralized multi-agent, balancing error control (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{e}=4.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{e}=4.4</annotation></semantics></math>) with manageable overhead; (3) <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Tool-heavy tasks</span> (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=16</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{SA}}=0.63" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>SA</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.63</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\text{SA}}=0.63</annotation></semantics></math>) favor decentralized multi-agent despite high overhead (263%), because parallelization and redundancy outweigh efficiency losses. Quantitatively, the decision boundary between single-agent and multi-agent is:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{SA}}^{*}=\frac{\hat{\beta}_{4}}{\hat{\beta}_{17}}\approx\frac{0.063}{0.408}=0.154\quad\text{(in standardized units)}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mtext>SA</mtext><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>4</mn></msub><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>17</mn></msub></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mn>0.063</mn><mn>0.408</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0.154</mn></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>(in standardized units)</mtext></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\text{SA}}^{*}=\frac{\hat{\beta}_{4}}{\hat{\beta}_{17}}\approx\frac{0.063}{0.408}=0.154\quad\text{(in standardized units)},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.2" class="ltx_p">corresponding to raw performance <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx 0.45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.45</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 0.45</annotation></semantics></math> after denormalization. This threshold, derived purely from data, aligns with empirical best practices and offers the first <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">quantitative</span> criterion for coordination structure selection, replacing heuristic “<span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">when to use agents</span>”, and “<span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px7.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">which agentic architecture to use</span>” guidance with a predictive model. Cross-validation on held-out configurations confirms this rule achieves 87% correct architecture selection, substantially exceeding random choice (20%) or capability-only models (54%). The scaling principle thus constitutes both a scientific contribution–the first universal equation for agentic systems–and an engineering tool for resource-efficient deployment.</p>
</div>

AIC confirms superior model fit even after penalizing for additional parameters.</span></span></p></div></div>
